issue_context.title: ActiveSupport::MessageVerifier is broken if `ActiveSupport.use_standard_json_time_format = false`
issue_context.body:
This PR https://github.com/rails/rails/pull/37983

specifically this line: https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/557dbcf1ed5a73420fb41f5899bce28ef0a21373#diff-a40dd89507c50053b464ecefd717f343R10

assumes that `expires_at` is in ISO 8601 format.
However, it isn't always this case if `ActiveSupport.use_standard_json_time_format = false` because `Time#as_json` would return a non ISO 8601 string thus breaking the message verifier.

### Steps to reproduce

```ruby
# frozen_string_literal: true

require 'bundler/inline'

gemfile(true) do
  source 'https://rubygems.org'

  git_source(:github) { |repo| "https://github.com/#{repo}.git" }

  # Activate the gem you are reporting the issue against.
  gem 'activesupport', '6.0.3'
end

require 'active_support'
require 'active_support/core_ext/object/blank'
require 'active_support/json'
require 'minitest/autorun'

class MessageVerifierTest < Minitest::Test
  def test_message_verifier
    ActiveSupport.use_standard_json_time_format = false
    verifier = ActiveSupport::MessageVerifier.new("Hey, I'm a secret!")

    assert_equal 'hi', verifier.verify(verifier.generate('hi', expires_at: Time.now.utc + 10))
  end
end

```

### Expected behavior
It works.

### Actual behavior
It raises an exception:

```
Minitest::UnexpectedError: ArgumentError: invalid date: "2020/06/05 17:44:39 +0000
```

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 6.0.3

**Ruby version**: 2.6.3

You might consider reducing complexity by having your parse method handle whatever value is being assigned.

```ruby
          return expires_at unless expires_at.is_a?(String)
          return Time.iso8601(expires_at) if ActiveSupport.use_standard_json_time_format
          Time.parse(expires_at)
```
@allolex No. The implemented version looks simple to read.
